ai.description: This slender, cylindrical snake reaches 20–25 cm. It is uniform dark brown to black with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include 20 midbody scale rows and a rounded, blunt head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlops tenuicollis* is best distinguished by its exceptionally slender, thread-like body and a distinctively narrow, elongated head that lacks a sharp rostral keel.
ai.habitat: *Indotyphlops tenuicollis* inhabits moist, forested regions of the Indian subcontinent, typically found in leaf litter or soil at moderate to high altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Samagutin Worm Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending much of its time burrowing through loose soil or leaf litter in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Samagutin Worm Snake is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of elongated eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, often between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlops tenuicollis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
